3090168.findings: One photo of four glass vases, no marks, labels or signatures visible and no bases shown. Left: footed trumpet vase in clear lead crystal with a ruby-red overlay oval cut back to clear with two perched birds and leaves, saw-tooth rim and star and hobnail cutting. This is the pattern normally sold as Hofbauer 'Byrdes' (German), but no Hofbauer mark is visible so that is attribution by style only. Centre: moulded pale lavender-tinted vase with frosted floral and leaf panels and a wavy rim (looks like modern pressed glass). Right: large cut or pressed crystal fan vase on a star-cut foot, plus a miniature fan vase. Nothing here suggests an under-described or rare piece.
3090168.condition: No chips or cracks visible in the single photo, but the saw-tooth rims and bases are not shown close up.
3090168.reason: Mass-market cut crystal and moulded glass; the ruby bird vase is common Hofbauer Byrdes style with no mark visible, low value.

3090169.findings: Silver plated serving ware: large two-handled rectangular tray with shell and scroll border and engraved foliate centre; footed two-handled soup tureen with domed lid, pineapple or acorn style finial and a matching shell-bowl ladle (photo 2 shows the tureen body without its lid); oval entree dish with pressed glass liner and an engraved domed cover with scroll handle. No hallmarks, EPNS stamps or maker's marks visible because no bases or undersides were photographed. The only writing is on paper consignor tags (tray tag number reads 4711 or 1174 depending on orientation, other tags handwritten and illegible), which are not marks. Plated, not sterling, going by the title and the worn finish.
3090169.condition: General tarnish, light scratching and wear to the tray centre and plating wear on high points; glass liner looks intact; no dents seen.

3090170.findings: Seven items. Two cream and brown bud vases with brown fish designs (1950s-60s Japanese export look), one with a gold foil oval sticker that is mostly illegible (only '...IZAN' partly readable). A Vietnamese or Chinese style blue and white crackle-glazed bottle vase with chrysanthemum and leaf bands (modern decorative look). An octagonal Indian dish in tinned copper or white metal with engraved all-over foliage and heavy oxidation. A deep blue crystalline-glaze studio bowl with a dark exterior: the title attributes it to Cath Wyllie, but no base or mark was photographed so that is unverified. A web search (printsandprintmaking.gov.au/artists/21175, searched 19/10/2026) lists a Cath Wyllie as a Tasmanian ceramic artist who worked at the Tin Sheds studio in Launceston in the 1990s; I found no sale prices or exhibition record for her. Also a small Japanese orange dragonware (moriage dragon) vase with a green neck and a Japanese blue and white camellia dish with a brown rim. No maker's marks readable on any piece.
3090170.condition: No chips or cracks visible in the photos; the Indian dish is mottled and oxidised; bases and rims not shown close up.
3090170.reason: Mixed decorative oriental pieces; the only named maker is the crystalline bowl (Cath Wyllie, a minor Launceston studio potter, unverified, base not shown), modest value.
3090170.marks_read: gold foil export sticker on fish vase, mostly illegible ('...IZAN'); no potter's mark seen

3090176.findings: Ten loose items; the title mentions only the Portuguese pitcher and Israeli glass bowl. Best piece is a flower-encrusted lidded vase (pot pourri or sugar form) with hand-modelled applied roses, poppies, forget-me-nots and a tulip finial, a pierced cover, gilt scalloped rim and scroll feet, in the style of Coalport or Rockingham 'Coalbrookdale' encrusted porcelain of about 1830-50 (could be a later copy); no mark is visible and the base was not photographed, so maker and age are unverified. Also a cobalt blue and gilt English-style porcelain footed sugar bowl with floral panels and scroll handles (lid missing); a Portuguese-style jug with a stylised blue and red bird and flowers (no mark visible); a frosted grey-lilac Israeli glass bowl with drip decoration (no signature seen); an amethyst glass ball; a modern red carved-resin lacquer apple box and a red resin sleeping boy figure; a small cast metal imp figure with a peg (looks like a bottle opener or fitting); and a brass cockerel. No marks or signatures readable in any photo.
3090176.condition: The encrusted vase looks intact with no obvious flower losses in the photos, though small petal chips are hard to rule out; the cobalt bowl has rim staining, gilt wear and no lid; the other items look sound.
3090176.reason: Title hides a hand-modelled flower-encrusted lidded porcelain vase in Coalport/Rockingham style (unmarked in photos, base not shown) plus a cobalt and gilt Victorian-style bowl; worth a base check.

3090177.findings: Three frames and philatelic items: a bi-fold double frame in brass tone with cream backing, a small silvered or white metal frame with ornate corners and a twisted rope border, and a larger brass-tone frame with embossed corners and domed glass. 3090177.marks_read: cover and stamp inscriptions only (Terra Australis, Australia, Brisbane Qld cancel)

3090179.findings: Fine Japanese Satsuma-type earthenware tea set, probably Meiji export (about 1880-1910), with crisp painting of bamboo groves and flying sparrows, raised gold gilt on the foliage and gilt rims; cream crackled glaze with pink-tinged cup interiors. Pieces seen: teapot (gilt ball finial), covered sugar bowl (orange-red ball finial, two small loop handles), covered milk jug (orange-red ball finial), 3 cups with 3 saucers, and 1 extra saucer or side plate on a stand (10 pieces). The title mentions no maker. Photos 4 and 5 show a rectangular gold-on-black cartouche on the cup base with two characters that appear to read 光山 (Kozan); this is read from the photos only, and the Kozan name was used by several Meiji workshops, so the maker is not confirmed. Rough comparable seen: Gorringes (Lewes) sale of 28 June 2022, lot 133, Kinkozan Meiji Satsuma tea wares (teapot, sugar pot, milk jug, four cups and saucers), estimate GBP 300 to 500, sold for GBP 950, with one chipped cup and a riveted sugar lid (https://auction.gorringes.co.uk/auction-lot-detail/LJUNE22/133, fetched 19/10/2026). That set had different decoration and four-character Kinkozan style marks, so it is only a guide.
3090179.condition: Sold as is. Visible: a small rim chip on one saucer at about 9 o'clock (photo 4); light gilt wear on some rims and handle tips; the teapot spout tip looks intact with a gilt rim. No cracks seen on the visible surfaces, but hairlines, cup interiors, lid fit and the undersides of the other pieces are not shown. Incomplete set (one cup short of the saucers).
3090179.reason: Fine Meiji-style Satsuma tea set with gilt bamboo and sparrow painting and a gold-on-black two-character signature cartouche (appears 光山, read from photos), 10 pieces, sold as is; a comparable Satsuma set made GBP 950 at Gorringes in 2022.
3090179.marks_read: gold-on-black cartouche on cup bases, two characters apparently 光山 (Kozan)

3090180.condition: Tray: cane floor split with several holes and missing strands, metal oxidised. Lantern: brass has an aged patina with some corrosion, glass looks intact with no chips seen, wiring is a yellow cord that probably needs replacing.
3090180.reason: Damaged cane and metal tray plus an unmarked brass and glass hall lantern, modest value.

3090181.findings: A handwritten card (photo 2) reads: 1824 letter written to John Bailey Esqr from Solicitor Wm S. Hesleden of Barton-Upon-Humber, Lincolnshire, regarding property matters of Barton Estate and Lord Middleton. The letter itself is a folded stampless cover addressed to 'Jno Burley Esqr, 8 New Square, Lincolns Inn, London' (the handwriting looks like Burley rather than Bailey), with a straight-line BARTON handstamp, a circular date stamp, remains of a seal, a manuscript docket and the date 5 June 1824; it is signed W. S. Hesleden, Barton 5th June 1824, and discusses the Burley Estate (rental about 2000 pounds a year), a Yorkshire estate (about 1500 pounds a year), Lord Middleton and a settlement or mortgage. Also a plain tan leather document wallet with two press studs and an inner metal clip, and a small crocodile-pattern leather purse with a metal clasp. No maker's stamps or labels visible on either leather item.
3090181.condition: Letter: browned, foxed and fold-worn, with a small hole in the second page where the seal was, but legible. Wallet: scuffed with worn edges. Purse: crocodile pattern worn at the corners.
3090181.reason: 1824 estate letter of some local historical interest but modest value, plus plain unmarked leather wallets.
3090181.marks_read: BARTON handstamp, circular datestamp, manuscript date 5 June 1824, signed W S Hesleden; no maker marks on leather
